full_judgment: 2. Short facts, relevant for the purpose of disposal of this Rule, are that one Md Moniruzzaman Khan, Anti-Corruption Officer, Anti-Corruption Bureau, Dhaka as informant lodged a First Information Report (in brief the FIR) Area, Dhaka with the Sutrapur Police Station being No. 62 dated 29-1-2008 under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860 against the accused-petitioner. The allegation inter alia was that at the time of inquiry of nothi No. 347-2000 the informant came to know that one Srimoti Trinoyni Das, wife of late Sudhir Chandra Das, 48 North Blockhall Road, Police Station-Sutrapur, District-Dhaka was the owner of 0.1140 acres of land in plot No. 1056 of SA Khatian No. 624 under Sutrapur Mouza, Dhaka. At the time of her death in the year 1972 she had no successor in Bangladesh. Therefore, the Government of Bangladesh became the owner of the said 0.1140 acres of land along with her all other properties. But after the death of the Srimoti Treenoney Das, Md Abul Kashem Howlader son of Abul Zalil Howlader created a forged sale deed being No. 1228 dated 28-6-1997. Thereafter he used the said deed before the Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kotwali Circle on 21-8-1991 a in Namjari Case No. 773(Su)/91-92. The accused Md Abul Kashem by using that deed got the residence No. 68-69, Paridash Road measuring 0.0400 acres of land mutated in his name. The accused thereby committed offence under sections 420/467/468/471 of the Penal Code, 1860.
